sections.h2: Which Clay County offices deal with property tax?
sections.html:
Responsibility in Clay County splits into three. One office, the Property Valuation Administrator, puts a worth on each parcel. The Sheriff prints the bills and collects. The County Clerk accepts appeal papers and eventually receives any bill the sheriff couldn't collect. Knowing which desk owns which question saves a seller several wrong-number calls.

All three share one building, 102 Richmond Road in Manchester. Don't bring a check to the PVA: it sets no tax rate and takes no payments, and its job stops at the number on the roll.

Clay County property tax contacts

Clay County covers 471 square miles of Appalachian hills, with Manchester at the center. The 2020 count was 20,345 people, and the July 2025 estimate of 19,465 is 4.3 percent lower, so a listing draws from a shrinking local pool.

There are 7,288 households living in 8,781 housing units, and owners head 76.4 percent of them. The typical home value is $90,700. Typical rent is $724 a month, and typical monthly owner cost is $978 with a mortgage and $367 without. With prices in that range, unpaid tax takes a noticeable bite out of your net, so learn the balance before you pick an asking price.

sections.h2: How the PVA values a house
sections.html:
Every assessment is anchored to January 1. The standard is fair cash value, the price a willing buyer and seller with full information would agree on. Every parcel gets a staff visit at least once per four years, and new construction is added annually.

A recent purchase can simplify things. Bought last year? Your deed price can become next January's value provided the building is unchanged. Frankfort assesses only public service companies, bank shares, omitted tangible property and vehicles, and the local PVA handles all other real and personal property.

Beyond the annual value, the PVA's office follows ownership changes, maintains parcel maps, updates building details and administers exemptions on real estate. Before listing, ask staff three things: does the map show your true acreage, does the building file include a finished basement or a shed that's gone, and does the exemption record still fit the owner.

Errors in those records flow straight into the bill. A garage that came down years ago but still sits on the record keeps lifting the value until someone asks for a correction. Stop in on a weekday between 8:00 and 4:30, or mail the office at 102 Richmond Road, Suite 200, Manchester, KY 40962.

Collection runs from fall into spring under the sheriff. Parcel lookups sit behind a View Property Tax Bill button on the sheriff's page of the Fiscal Court site. For the exact opening date, ring 606-598-3471, because the state allows 30-day phases when a county needs another calendar.

Under the standard pattern:

  • October 1 to November 1: 2 percent off
  • November 2 to December 31: face amount
  • January: 5 percent added
  • February 1 to April 15: 21 percent added

Because value freezes on January 1, a mid-year sale can leave the old owner's name on the bill.

Follow these steps in order. Skip one and you're out.

  • Watch for the notice the PVA mails after raising a value.
  • Ask the PVA or a deputy for a conference while the roll is open for inspection: two weeks, Monday through Saturday, beginning the first Monday of May.
  • If talks fail, file the appeal paper with the County Clerk by close of business the next workday after the window ends.
  • Attend the local board hearing, held 25 to 35 days after inspection. The board gets five sitting days unless the state grants more.
  • Bring proof: sales of similar houses, an appraisal, or building costs. With no facts, the board has to deny you.

Filing without showing up for the hearing forfeits your right to go further. After the board rules, you can still take the case to the Kentucky Board of Tax Appeals.

The exemption goes to residents of the home who are 65 or older, or classified as totally disabled. For assessment years 2025 and 2026 the amount is $49,100, taken off the valuation before tax is figured.

The application goes to the PVA in Manchester, 606-598-3832. To prove age, use a driver's license, birth certificate or passport. A disability claim needs paperwork from the federal agency or retirement system that made the classification. Most disability claims renew annually. Exceptions cover owners with a service-connected disability and owners ruled permanently disabled by Social Security or Kentucky Retirement Systems.

sections.h2: What happens to an unpaid bill
sections.html:
At close of business on April 15 the sheriff passes the bill to the County Clerk, where it turns into a certificate of delinquency and a lien against the parcel. Interest starts at 1 percent a month, with 10 percent more for the clerk and 20 percent for the county attorney.

The county attorney writes to owners in May and, if necessary, June, and can arrange installments. From mid-July, certificates may be sold to outside buyers through late October. After a sale you owe the buyer, and more fees follow. The County Clerk's website posts a delinquent tax page for each year, which is the place to check whether a parcel was advertised for sale.

The Fiscal Court website, claycountyky.com, has a page for each department with contact details and hours, and the sheriff's page holds the bill lookup. The County Clerk's own site lists Recordings, Fees, Forms and an Open Records Request page.

sections.h2: Handling the tax bill when you sell
sections.html:
Normally the closing agent pays this year's bill from your proceeds and prorates it with the buyer. Any open delinquency comes first, since the lien stays on the land. Request a payoff from the sheriff before you sign, and check with the PVA on whether an exemption ends at transfer.

The deed adds a separate charge. Kentucky taxes the seller $0.50 for every $500 slice of the price, and a partial slice counts in full. The clerk takes it at the recording counter. Foreclosure deeds, divorce transfers, correction deeds and nominal gifts between parent and child fall outside the tax.

Put these on your list in the weeks before closing: the sheriff's payoff, the clerk's total if any bill is delinquent, and the amount of deed tax. Having each number on paper early keeps the closing date from slipping.

faqs.q: Who mails the Clay County tax bill?
faqs.a: The Sheriff. If nothing shows up in your mailbox, phone 606-598-3471 or search the parcel online.

faqs.q: Can a Clay County owner contest a value in summer?
faqs.a: Generally no. Both the conference and the clerk filing must land in the May inspection window, with the filing due the next workday after it ends. Phone the PVA at 606-598-3832 in spring.

faqs.q: Does the Clay County PVA take tax payments?
faqs.a: No. That office only values property and processes exemptions. Money goes to the sheriff, then to the County Clerk after mid-April.

faqs.q: Is transfer tax owed on a Clay County sale?
faqs.a: Typically, and the seller pays it: $0.50 per $500 of price, collected by the clerk at recording. Foreclosure deeds, divorce transfers and correction deeds are exempt.

faqs.q: Can a Clay County house with a delinquent bill still be sold?
faqs.a: Yes. Pay the delinquency at or before closing, and ask the County Clerk for the full total with interest and fees so the payoff is right.
